objects: For measures μ,ν on E, a coupling is exactly a measure γ on E×E with first projection pushforward μ and second projection pushforward ν. The supplied coupling set consists of all such γ. For κ:E×E→[0,∞], define C_κ(μ,ν)=inf{∫⁻ κ(z) dγ(z) : γ is such a coupling}, with the infimum and nonnegative integral both valued in the extended nonnegative reals. In particular, the infimum of an empty feasible set is ∞; attainment is not part of the definition. Write μ_t=(X(t,·))#P. The probability-measure map is explicitly supplied with the measurable proof hX(t), so its function is X(t,·); at p and q it uses hX(Prod.fst p) and hX(Prod.fst q). Let κ₂(z)=(ι(c(z)))², where ι:[0,∞)→[0,∞] is the coercion. Define D(t,s)=Real.sqrt(ENNReal.toReal(C_κ₂(μ_t,μ_s))). This is a real-valued expression, not an asserted metric. The order is: coerce the pointwise cost to ENNReal and square it; integrate and infimize to obtain the ENNReal transport cost; apply ENNReal.toReal; then apply Real.sqrt. The other data are U:T×E→F and L∈ℝ.
domains: T is a topological space with FirstCountableTopology. Ω is a measurable space and P is a probability measure on Ω. E is a compact topological space with a measurable space; every open subset of the topological product E×E is assumed measurable for the product measurable structure. The statement does not require that this structure equal a Borel sigma-algebra, nor impose Hausdorffness, metrizability, or first-countability on E. F is a normed additive commutative group, with no assumed scalar-vector-space structure or completeness. X:T→Ω→E; c is a continuous map E×E→NNReal, thus finite and nonnegative; U:T×E→F; L is real. No measurable structure on T or topology on Ω is required.
quantifiers: Universally quantify T, Ω, E, F and all listed structures, then P, X, the proof that every slice is measurable, the almost-sure path-continuity proof, c, and the proof that c vanishes on the diagonal. Then universally choose U and L, and assume one bound quantified over every ordered pair p,q∈T×E using that same L. For every such collection of data conclude Continuous U.
assumptions: For every t∈T the slice X(t,·) is measurable. For P-almost every ω the whole path t↦X(t,ω) is continuous on T. For every x∈E, c(x,x)=0. For every t,s∈T and x,y∈E, ‖U(t,x)−U(s,y)‖ ≤ L·(Real.sqrt(ENNReal.toReal(C_κ₂(μ_t,μ_s))) + (c(x,y):ℝ)). Compactness, first-countability and product-open-set measurability are as stated in the domains slot. There is no separate assumption L≥0, no preexisting measurability or continuity hypothesis on U, no joint-measurability hypothesis on X, and no symmetry, triangle inequality, or separation axiom for c. No separate finite-cost or optimal-coupling premise is stated.
conclusion: U:T×E→F is continuous jointly for the product topology on T×E and the norm topology on F.
scopes: The norm bound is pointwise and global for all pairs of time-state arguments. It is neither an almost-everywhere bound nor restricted to a time horizon. Only the whole-path continuity premise is P-almost everywhere; slice measurability holds for every time and c vanishes at every diagonal point. The conclusion is continuity everywhere of the deterministic map U, not merely along sample paths or separately in each variable. The marginal order in the transport expression is μ_t first and μ_s second. The raw signature specifically uses Real.sqrt after ENNReal.toReal, and does not use an ENNReal square-root operation. ENNReal.toReal is total, with toReal(∞)=0; this convention is retained without adding a finite-value assumption.
constant_dependencies: L is a single fixed real number controlling all pairs p,q, chosen after U and the preceding probability, process and cost data. It may depend on those chosen data but does not vary with p or q in the bound. Its sign is not separately constrained. No additional bound, rate, or continuity modulus is asserted.
